standard_prerequisites.name: Formation of Tor groups commutes with filtered colimits, and the quotient of the localization by the module can be written as the colimit of the quotients by the successive powers

standard_prerequisites.name: The tensor product of the ring modulo its power torsion with the second piece is the second piece modulo its own power torsion

standard_prerequisites.name: The long exact sequence of Tor groups attached to a short exact sequence, and the statement that the sequence of the glueing pair remains exact after tensoring
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the exact sequence whose first term vanishes by a previous lemma in the universal case, and keeps the presentation exact after tensoring in the general case.

core_obligations: Reduce to the case where the element is a nonzerodivisor on the module: replace the module by its quotient by its power torsion submodule, noting that this does not change the cokernel of the localization map, and write that cokernel as the colimit of the quotients by the successive powers (proof lines 25507-25515).

Further reduce to the universal example where the module is the ring modulo its power torsion: identify the tensor product of that example with the second piece, use the exact sequence of the glueing pair to display the exact sequence relating the first Tor group of the second piece with the quotient, observe that the connecting arrow is injective, and conclude that the group vanishes because the first term is zero by a previous lemma (proof lines 25517-25537).

Treat the general case: choose a surjection onto the module from a free module over the ring modulo its power torsion, form the displayed short exact sequence with the kernel, and use the statement that the sequence of the glueing pair remains exact after tensoring to conclude that the same sequence stays exact (proof lines 25539-25547).

Conclude that the first Tor group of the second piece with the quotient by the powers vanishes, since it vanishes for the free module by the previous paragraph and the sequence is exact, which finishes the proof (proof lines 25548-25550).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a nonzerodivisor and to the quotients by the individual powers (proof lines 25507-25515).
Solve the universal example with the long exact sequence of Tor and a previous vanishing statement (proof lines 25517-25537).
Pass to a general module through a free presentation whose sequence stays exact (proof lines 25539-25550).
difficulty_reason: The statement says that for a glueing pair the first Tor group of the second piece with the cokernel of the localization map of any module vanishes (statement lines 25498-25505). The proof reduces in two stages: first to the case where the element is a nonzerodivisor and to the quotients by the individual powers through the commutation of Tor with filtered colimits, and then to the universal example of the ring modulo its power torsion, where the exact sequence of the glueing pair together with a previously established vanishing and the injectivity of the connecting arrow gives the result, the general case following from a free presentation whose sequence remains exact after tensoring (proof lines 25507-25550). The two reductions and the exact sequence computation are the substance of the argument.
